answer: Each identity registers one key-bound watermark, signed by its quill key on the ledge, and locks a 90 bond. Each job carries it; the client checks before paying. The ledge groups watermarks by key hash; two identities sharing one mark collapse to one entry, losing payment. A forger thus needs a distinct watermark and paid work per fake identity: 90 bond plus 35 registration each, so 1,000 fakes lock 125,000 credit, no bulk discount; an honest agent pays 125 once. A watermark that wanders across identities fails: the check matches the mark to the delivery key, and a mismatch burns the bond.
